payload.claim: `peak_turns` is computed as `max(num_turns)` over every row `ledger.attempts(task_id)` returns (stack.py:136-138), with no filter on `phase`. For a layer that went through a revision, `ledger.open_attempt(task_id, phase="SPEC_REVIEW")` (saffron/batch.py:580) and `phase=spec_review.WRITING_PHASE` (saffron/batch.py:686-688) write attempts under the same `task_id`, bounded by their own ceilings (`SPEC_REVIEW_MAX_TURNS=90`, `SPEC_WRITER_MAX_TURNS=120` in saffron/spec_review.py), not by the spec's `max_turns`. The rendered line reads `<peak> of <max_turns> turns`, so a layer that only ran a few IMPLEMENT turns but went through one spec-review round can show a peak taken from that unrelated pre-cell session, against a ceiling that session was never bound by. The test fixture in tests/test_stack_view.py only ever calls the plain `_attempt` helper (no SPEC_REVIEW/SPEC_WRITING phase), so this never surfaces in the gates.
